listings.title: How Was the Cosmic Microwave Background Discovered?
listings.description:
In 1964, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson picked up a strange noise in their giant antenna. Pigeons were nesting inside, leaving droppings, but the noise was not the pigeons. It came from every direction in the sky: the afterglow of the Big Bang.

Sources:
APS, Holmdel horn antenna: https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/historic-sites/holmdel-horn-antenna
Nobel Prize, 1978 physics press release: https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1978/press-release/
AIP, Tools of Cosmology: https://history.aip.org/exhibits/cosmology/tools/tools-new.htm

listings.title: How Was Penicillin Discovered?
listings.description:
In 1928, Alexander Fleming returned from holiday to find mould on a dish of bacteria. Around the mould, the bacteria were dying. He called the mould juice penicillin; others later turned it into a medicine that has saved millions.

Sources:

listings.title: Who Discovered That Plants Produce Oxygen?
listings.description:
In 1771, Joseph Priestley put a sprig of mint into air in which a candle had burned out. Ten days later, a fresh candle burned perfectly well. This Short tells the story of his mint experiment.

Source:
Joseph Priestley, Observations on Different Kinds of Air: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/29734/29734-h/29734-h.htm

listings.title: Who First Measured Blood Pressure?
listings.description:
Stephen Hales measured blood pressure using a tall glass tube connected to a mare's artery. The blood rose about eight feet, rising and falling with each heartbeat. In 1733, he published the first blood pressure reading.

Sources:
University of Minnesota, Stephen Hales: http://www.epi.umn.edu/cvdepi/essay/reverend-stephen-hales-on-blood-pressure/
